messages.content:
You compare an edited output video against its actual source video, the original user request, and the executed editing instruction. Optional reference assets show the desired editing target.
The historical-source selection in the original user request has already been executed. Evaluate only its editing requirements against the actual videos. Do not treat historical appearance descriptions in that request as observed facts; use the visible source video instead. Compare the original editing requirements with the executed instruction too, so you can identify any omitted or changed constraint introduced when the instruction was normalized.
The output_video_card was produced earlier by independently observing only the output. Treat it as a fixed observation record: do not rewrite it, return a new card, or add intended changes to it. It can be imperfect; inspect the actual videos when comparing.
Call record_edit_result exactly once. Return only its five parameters: requested_change, observed_change, fulfillment, unexpected_changes, uncertain. These describe the source-to-output comparison, not a new video card. Use concise English.
State what was requested and what visibly changed. Use fulfillment=fulfilled, partial, not_fulfilled, or uncertain. Do not infer success from the instruction. Note unintended changes to identity, appearance, action, scene, camera, timing, and image quality when visible. If a reference match or subtle facial change cannot be judged, record the uncertainty rather than assuming success. Do not claim to have inspected missing reference pixels. Do not call an editing tool or regenerate video.
Use one separate XML parameter block for each of the five parameters. The three text parameters contain text. unexpected_changes and uncertain contain JSON arrays of strings, including [] when empty. Do not nest a card or review object inside any parameter.
Structural example only; replace descriptions with your actual comparison:
<tool_call>
<function=record_edit_result>
<parameter=requested_change>Requested edit</parameter>
<parameter=observed_change>Actual visible change</parameter>
<parameter=fulfillment>uncertain</parameter>
<parameter=unexpected_changes>[]</parameter>
<parameter=uncertain>["Any unresolved comparison"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

content.text: {"executed_editing_prompt":"Change the person's hairstyle to the one shown in the reference images, using the front view for the front styling and the back view for the back styling. Transfer only the hairstyle shape and structure from the references; do not adopt the reference person's facial features, hair color, or clothing. Preserve the person's original hair color, identity, and all other elements of the current video.","history_selection_status":"Already executed. Only compare editing requirements; historical appearance words are not observed facts.","original_user_request":"Using the provided source video, apply the following edit: I'd like to change the person's hairstyle to the one shown in the reference images. Only transfer the hairstyle from the reference images, not the reference person's facial features, hair color, or clothing. Preserve everything else in the current video.","output_video_card":{"observed":{"action":"The man stands on a stone patio, initially facing away, then turns his head and upper body to look over his left shoulder before turning back to face the water.","camera":"A static, medium full shot from behind the subject at a slightly low angle.","clothing":"A white sleeveless tank top with a green graphic on the lower back, light green shorts, and pink sneakers.","hair_color":"Black.","hairstyle":"Short, dark hair with a small top-knot or bun at the back of the head.","identity":"A muscular man with a dark complexion, seen mostly from behind.","scene":"An outdoor stone terrace overlooking a calm ocean under a clear blue sky, with rocks and wooden posts visible in the water."},"uncertain":[]}}

arguments.observed_change: The person's hair changed from a high ponytail/bun to a shorter, flatter style with a small top knot and more closely cropped sides, matching the reference structure more closely. The rest of the scene, clothing, action, and camera framing appear unchanged.
arguments.requested_change: Change the person's hairstyle to the reference style, transferring only shape and structure while preserving original hair color, identity, clothing, and all other video elements.
uncertain: Whether the original hair color was fully preserved in all frames, since the head is often backlit and details are limited.
